title: Error Propagation & Significant Figures Rules
notes: Significant figures communicate measurement precision. In 0.00450 m there are three significant figures: leading zeros locate the decimal; the final zero after the decimal is significant.
For multiplication or division, round the final result to the fewest significant figures among measured inputs. For addition or subtraction, round to the least precise decimal place.
Example: 2.34×1.2=2.808 rounds to 2.8 (two significant figures). But 12.11+0.3=12.41 rounds to 12.4 (one decimal place).
Keep guard digits in intermediate steps and round once at the end. Exact counts and defined conversion factors do not limit significant figures.
For powers, propagate measurement uncertainty before rounding: if A=πr², a 1% uncertainty in r gives approximately 2% uncertainty in A.
confusion: Do not apply the fewest-significant-figures rule to addition.
Exact counted values do not impose measurement precision.
